newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - U.S. acquisition boosts Dutch Ahold.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. acquisition boosts Dutch Ahold.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Koninklijke Ahold NV announced sharply higher third quarter net profits on Wednesday, largely due to extra sales after a major U.S. acquisition this summer.
Net profit jumped to 156.4 million guilders($91.41 million) from 101.6 million guilders as the $2.9 billion acquisition of Stop & Shop in July made its first contribution.
Ahold said 1996 full-year net earnings would be significantly higher than last year.
"Further growth of earnings per share is expected to be positively influenced by the acquisition of Stop & Shop," Ahold said in a statement.
Third quarter turnover rose 33.7 percent to 9.27 billion guilders while operating profit surged 45.8 percent to 307.6 million guilders.
In addition to the Stop & Shop acquisition, Ahold benefitted from a stronger dollar which was worth 1.68 guilders in the third quarter of 1996, versus 1.61 a year earlier.
Since the Stop & Shop acquisition over half of Ahold's sales are generated in the United States.
Ahold's third-quarter profits were in line with analysts' forecasts of 134 to 170 million guilders, but analysts were no particularly enthusiatic.
"At first sight, they look like very decent numbers... We were quite satisfied, but (they're) nothing spectacular," said Lidy Knigge, of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
Ahold has recently stated its aim to become the world's biggest supermarket organisation in five to 10 years through continuing expansion in the world's fastest-growing economies.
Ahold has expanded into Asia this year, setting up joint ventures in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and China.
And in November, the group announced plans to take a 50 percent stake in Brazilian supermarket chain Bompreco, its first foray into South America.
In Amsterdam, Ahold shares closed 3.40 guilders lower at 102.90 guilders.
